title: Sunrise Direction Compass: Where the Sun Rises
description: Find the compass direction of sunrise for your place and date with the Sunrise Direction Compass — degrees from north, season swing included. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, from New York the Sun rises at 58° in June (northeast-ish) but at 122° in December (southeast-ish) — a 63-degree swing along your horizon every year.
quick_answer: The Sunrise Direction Compass gives the compass bearing of sunrise for your place and date — where on the horizon the Sun will appear, in degrees from true north. Check it before you pick the viewpoint or align the photo.

Avenues and avenues of stones align on specific dates (Manhattanhenge is the famous grid case). The compass finds which dates your street catches.
Which windows get dawn light in June versus December is this bearing, read at both solstices.
Facing the dawn or avoiding its glare on the trail — know the bearing before the boots.
Around March 20 and September 22 the Sun rises at almost exactly 90° — due east — nearly everywhere on Earth (90.6° computed for New York on March 20). Every other date drifts from that anchor.
New York: 58.3° (June) and 121.6° (December). London swings wider: June sunrise at 50.3°, closing on northeast — higher latitude, longer lean.

faq: To the standard algorithm's precision for the Sun's centre at a level horizon — within a fraction of a degree. Your hill, tower or treeline decides what you actually see, and when.
Why doesn't the Sun rise due east?
Earth's tilt gives the Sun a seasonal declination; the rise point slides along the horizon toward the summer pole's side. Due east happens only at the equinoxes.
True. A physical compass needs the local declination added — the True North vs Magnetic page on this site handles the conversion.
By symmetry: 360° minus the sunrise figure. The Sun Azimuth Calculator tracks the bearing all day if you need the full sweep.
How wide is the Sun itself?
About half a degree across — 'first gleam' and 'full disc up' differ by that much bearing and a couple of minutes.
Bearings swing wildly and, inside the circles, the Sun may not rise or set at all on your date — the Polar Day / Night Checker rules there.
The seasons swap: December brings the northern-style northern sunrise. The compass computes your hemisphere as it finds it.
Can I find the date the Sun rises over a landmark?
Read the landmark's bearing from your spot, then scan dates until the compass matches it — the alignment-date hunt in one loop.
